target.approved: owner 2026-11-19: one real doorway into Building 1 and this one interior (hall, mural and bar)

evidence.hall_photos: five web photos of the hall (photos 1-5), 18 Jul 2023 (from their metadata), kept outside Git and used only to measure and match colours. 18 mm on an APS-C crop (20 mm for photo 2), perspective-corrected (vertical) with lens correction: level cameras about 1.5 m high, horizontal field 63.7 degrees
evidence.text: National Register nomination NRIS 08000081 (2007-12-02), Section 7 pages 3-4: entrance doors, marble-walled vestibule, three-storey concourse about 48 ft 8 in wide and 200 ft long, mural on most of the east wall, balcony with bronze Art Deco balustrade and tall square wood-clad columns over the vestibule, stairs at the north and south ends, wood panelling, terrazzo floor, chandeliers
evidence.bar_photos: two web photos of the bar room, no reuse licence, proportions only, kept outside Git
evidence.mural_size: about 250 ft by 26 ft (76 x 8 m), from a self-guided tour flyer for the building; the 2023 photos show it from the north gallery's end to the end of east bay 9 (photo 1's south end; the north end is provisional)
evidence.measurement: Heights and the east wall's rhythm come from level-camera fits to the 2023 photos (east pier corners, bases, band and mural top): thirteen equal east bays, office bays 3.6 m, band to 4.2 m, mural to 12.2 m, hall lanterns over every other east bay on the centre line at about 7.8-9.8 m, flat ceiling about 13 m. The window heads (exterior, 15.75 m over the floor) set the higher ceiling over the balcony. Round 3: a joint fit of the west and south views (photos 3 and 5: column side and hall faces, plinth bases, east piers) gives the colonnade's hall faces 35.2-35.5 m from the crescent's centre, the columns 0.5 m wide and 0.8 m deep; the stepped drum's front edge silhouettes 3.45 m into the hall (photo 5); the north view's camera stands about 2 m north of the old north line, under a gallery that crosses the hall's north end to the mural's start (photos 1, 4, 5).

north_annex.note: North of the old north line (the crescent's outer pier 0): the floor where the north view's camera stands, under a plain gallery up to its ceiling under the two-storey roof (14.75 m), its west side clear of the north junction's facade. Photo 4 shows only the balcony curving into the mural's start beside a narrow plaster return: the gallery across the north end is inferred (owner's shot list), its east end curving into the east wall below the mural's start (gallery_fillet, radius m).

plan_production_inference_m.note: Polar plan about the circle fitted to the exact crescent (runs 21-37). The hall runs between the radial lines of the outer crescent piers 0 and 11; the west colonnade stands on the facade's twelve pier lines, the east wall has its own thirteen equal bays over the same arc (2023 photos). Width 48 ft 8 in between the column faces and the east pier faces (NRHP).

heights_production_inference_m.note: Floor 2.5 cm over the highest drawn ground under it (6.495, the plaza over the land by the bar room's north wall; headless_interior_ground_contract.gd checks every floor sample). The door's sill (sill_y) stays 2.5 cm over the highest drawn ground at the door (6.345, at the vestibule's south-front corner): the vestibule's floor runs level with it for sill_landing (0.3 m) inside the door, then rises 1.9 degrees to the hall's floor at the colonnade's back; the open leaves reach past the landing, so their far ends sit over the start of the ramp. The sill's front is seen as a 45-degree bevel (threshold_bevel: its rise and run) and walked as a gentler hidden slope through the bevel's foot (threshold_walk: its slope, and how far it runs on under the foot, below the paving): the stock player's capsule reads a slope's top edge up to about 5 degrees steeper than the slope (Godot meets each collision triangle's edge on its own, within the 1 mm collision margin), so the bevel walked as seen read 48.6 degrees there, past the controller's 48-degree floor limit, and stopped about one walking approach in six at the doorstep (owner, 2026-11-21); 35 degrees reads at most about 41. The west heights are measured in the west and south views (photos 3 and 5, independent cameras): the openings' heads about 3.5 m, the reeded fascia about 3.8-4.0 m, the parapet's top 5.2-5.3 m and the Deco rail's 5.7-5.9 m. The walkway behind the parapet is unphotographed: level with its top, just over the vestibule's ceiling, which clears the facade's door transom (11.53 m); the open rail is solid to the player up to its top (railing); the north gallery's front is solid to the player from its floor to its ceiling, so the gallery is seen over its rail, never entered. The balcony zone's ceiling clears the tall windows' heads (22.12 m).

window.note: Inside, the tall windows show narrower than the facade's glass (photo 3): the same centres, a 1.9 m opening in a deep white reveal, three panes with paired mullions, five glazing bars with small squares where they cross the mullions.

door.note: The middle of the crescent's three door groups (the NRHP's main public entrance; its centre group under the canopy) opens: its three bronze leaves stand swung in against the reveal sides, the transom stays glazed.

rooms.note: West ground floor (2023 views; the west view's camera fitted on its columns): the vestibule in the door bay; the bar's blank room behind bays 7-9, open in bay 9 and curtained in 7-8, with curtained bay 6 north of it (the south view sees its curtain too); bay 10 a plain closed front (unphotographed); the north bays open into a plain room (the north view sees an open room there). East (13 bays): office bays with light doors and small high windows as photographed, the basement stair bay 5, the museum's open bays 7-9 with daylight at the back. The mural runs from the north gallery's end, beside a narrow plaster return (photo 4), to the south corner of the curved east wall, beside another (photos 5 and 2, and the 2019 view of its end, LR-5). Bays 10-12 below the band, the north annex and the south end wall stay plain (owner's shot list).

mural.note: Stage 2 (owner 2026-11-19): an original sea-animal mural after the layout of the hall's 1975 mural (credited under Murals; game/resources/textures/world/b1_hall/PROVENANCE.md), four tiles north to south meeting at its quarter points. Its scenes keep the scale they were painted at, 250 ft (design_length, m) less the calm sea and sky at each end (calm, a fraction of the picture), which take up the rest of the wall. The tiles load after play starts within load_radius (m) of the door and are released after unload_delay (s) beyond unload_radius (Building1MuralLoader).

reflections.note: Building1HallReflections, desktop (Forward+) only: real reflections in the polished floor, mode "inside" (while the camera is in the hall; the owner chose it for desktop, 2026-11-20), "always" (captures) or "off"; the build fails on any other mode. While on: the environment's screen-space reflections with ssr's settings (no fade at contact, long rays kept), the terrazzo polished (floor: roughness, specular, an albedo tint per channel; baked_sheen false puts up the floor's attributes without the painted streaks the real reflections replace), and with probes on, box-projected reflection probes along the crescent that see and reflect on the interior layer only (intensity: their share of the floor's reflection where the screen has nothing to reflect; blend: metres over which neighbours fade into each other). Without the probes the polished floor reflects the sky's radiance wherever SSR finds nothing on screen: the first trial's milky floor. Specular sets the grazing reflectance too (Godot's f90 = 50 f0, capped at 1): below 0.354 the whole reflection scales with its square at every angle, and 0.296 is the owner's 70% step of 0.45 (2026-11-20). The web's renderer has none of it and keeps the floor's polish baked into its vertex shading.

palette.note: Albedo times the baked vertex shading (building_1_interior.gd _shade): the sky's ambient light is all the hall gets by day, blue from above and warm from below, so floors run warmer and ceilings cooler than they read in the photos (calibrated on photo 5's floor, ceiling and drum). Specular stays low: the sky is the only reflection source, so a glossy floor would read sky-blue (on desktop the hall's reflections, Building1HallReflections, give it reflections of its own). lamp and daylight glow (DaySun night roles: lamps lit at night, daylight panels out).
